hints: Let $u = \sin^2\theta$ to write the equation as a quadratic $4u^2 + 12u - 7 = 0$.
Take square roots to get $\sin\theta = \pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and find all 4 angles on $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Treat the equation as a quadratic in $\sin^2\theta$:
$$4(\sin^2\theta)^2 + 12(\sin^2\theta) - 7 = 0$$

Solve $\sin\theta = \pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ for all four quadrants in $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \implies \theta = 45^\circ, \quad 180^\circ - 45^\circ = 135^\circ$$
$$\sin\theta = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \implies \theta = 180^\circ + 45^\circ = 225^\circ, \quad 360^\circ - 45^\circ = 315^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Factorises quadratic to obtain $\sin^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}$ (M1). Solves for $\sin\theta = \pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ (M1). Obtains all four solutions $\theta = 45^\circ, 135^\circ, 225^\circ, 315^\circ$ with no extras in range (A1, A1).
